raw: {"analysis":"Response SRD provides a more comprehensive and accurate plan that addresses all critical constraints from the repository facts. It correctly identifies the irreversible truncation risk and mandates backup/restore procedures, handles the global temp table cleanup, addresses the flaky network check, and properly sequences the approval gates. Response GGT has some concerning gaps: it suggests stripping dependencies on the global temp table (which could alter execution semantics), proposes caching the production dataset (introducing untested variables), and its rollback drill only verifies the system stops before truncation rather than testing actual recovery procedures. SRD's treatment of the rollback protocol as a restore-from-backup operation is more realistic given the irreversibility constraint.","verdict":"SRD"}
